messages:
maria.s: :rotating_light: Observed node-flap in us-west-2-gpu-23 around now. Multiple runtime containers crashed during model reload. Pods restarted automatically but we've seen a pattern: container OOMs immediately followed by CUDA illegal memory access in the same kernel invocation. Collecting logs now, opening thread for triage and handoff.

sanjeev: copying logs i'm seeing on node: 
```
Nov 14 02:12:08 gpu-23 kubelet[...]: Container crash: oom killed
Nov 14 02:12:08 gpu-23 kubelet[...]: Pod restart backoff
Nov 14 02:12:09 kernel: [12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:01:00:0 has fallen off the bus.
Nov 14 02:12:09 kernel: [12345.678910] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, PID=3456: 
Nov 14 02:12:09 runtime: panic: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
stack: runtime.go:....
```
Looks like a race during model reload + paging of KV cache. Pod was running a large Llama variant, 2048 context, weight sharded across two GPUs.

olivia: noted. Are the affected pods all running the same model version / quantization profile? Could be a kernel bug triggered by a specific memory alignment pattern after eviction.

maria.s: yes, all running rwd-llama-v2-13b.fp16.q4_0 pinned to tag v2026-11-12. Workload: long-form generation with streaming and prefix KV caching. Latency spike ~11% p50 for the service; impact window started ~02:11 and flapped for ~6m. Affected customers: a handful of mid-size tenants with high concurrency, routed through dedicated pool us-west-2-dedicated-gpu-1.

chandra: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) cordon gpu-23 to stop new pods landing, 2) drain and restart to get fresh driver state, 3) temporarily route traffic to us-west-2-gpu-12 (fallback pool), 4) turn off hot KV cache writes during reloads.

maria.s: doing cordon now.
`kubectl cordon gpu-23`
`kubectl get pods -o wide | grep gpu-23`

deploy-bot: Incident created INC-4479 (severity: P2). Auto-run: traffic shift to fallback pool initiated (partial).

sanjeev: I ran journalctl and GPU driver logs show repeated "misaligned address" warnings right before the illegal memory access: 
```
[  12345.678900] kernel: BUG: misaligned address 0x7f8b1c3a4 at gpu_copy.c:456
[  12345.678910] NVRM: 0x00000000(0x0000) 0x0 0x0 0x0
```
Not classic OOM only. Something's writing a pointer that crosses a page boundary and the kernel driver is tripping. Might be nv driver + kernel mismatch or a race between page reclaim and GPU DMA.

olivia: can we check if page migration (live paging) was active? Any OOM killer messages for system memory? If page reclaim and GPU DMA coincide, you can get stale GPU pointers. Also check if we had an OS kernel update/hotpatch applied recently on gpu-23.

maria.s: no kernel upgrades in last 48h on gpu-23. Paging/hugepage churn is high (we're seeing many small allocations from the serving runtime during reload).

chandra: immediate mitigation plan: 
- Drain gpu-23, restart nvidia-driver pods / host driver if in use.
- Re-deploy the model with smaller init batch so it doesn't prefetch entire KV cache. (reduce worker.concurrency and initial_prefetch=0)
- Toggle fallback to CPU-only model for affected tenants where latency is OK to avoid GPU crashes.

sanjeev: commands I executed: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service
kubectl rollout restart ds/gpu-device-plugin -n kube-system
```
After restart, one node rebooted cleanedly, another still shows kernel misaligned warnings in dmesg.

olivia: we should also add a temporary kernel module option: disable page migration for GPU buffers if driver supports it (nv-p2p/disable_migrate=1) - might be disruptive but reduces race surface. Coordinate with infra.

maria.s: i've opened a ticket to infra for kernel/driver flag change. Tagging @chandra for escalation if infra needs a backport.

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered for model v2026-11-12 -> v2026-11-10 on us-west-2-dedicated-gpu-1 (partial).

chandra: customer impact summary for support: 
- Scope: ~7 pods across 3 nodes in us-west-2 dedicated pool. 
- Symptoms: pod OOMs -> CUDA illegal memory access -> container crash -> restart. 
- User visible: transient 10-20% latency spikes and ~2-5% error rate on affected routes for ~6 minutes intermittently. 
- Mitigation: traffic shifted to fallback pool, kernels/drivers restarted, model rolled back to older tag, ongoing kernel flag evaluation.

olivia: next steps for oncall escalation: if dmesg still shows misaligned addresses after restart, prepare to capture a live repro: 
- Enable extra logging on runtime (RUNTIME_DEBUG=pagewalk:1)
- Collect coredump of crashed container: `kubectl get pods; kubectl cp pod:/var/crash/core /tmp`
- Capture `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DIAGNOSTIC` right after failure.

maria.s: doing handoff to olivia for hotpatch + infra coordination. I'm going offline for 30m after completing the traffic shift. Handing oncall to @olivia. :thumbsup:

olivia: ack. I'll own this and escalate to kernel team if we keep seeing misaligned traces. I'll also prepare a kernel repro job with a smaller synthetic workload to try to trigger the pointer misalignment under a controlled environment.

pagerduty: On-call alert acknowledged by olivia.

maria.s: thanks everyone. Will post post-incident summary after root cause confirmed and patch applied.

(Reaction notes: several thumbs up and :coffee: from infra and sde teams; temporary tags added: incident/P2, cuda/illegal-memory, paging/kvcache)
